1.text:
The new chapter begins with three letters and no sentence. "Alif-Lãm-Mĩm" is written in the chapter as it is recited, and the sources discuss what an opening of that kind does, since a hearer is given letters he already knows and no statement built out of them, which is why one source reads the letters as a demonstration of an inability, the Arabs being asked to bring a chapter like this book and unable to do it while the material of the book is their own speech. Another reads them as a summons to attend, a way of stopping a listener at the door of what follows, and an account preserves a reciter telling his people that God informed him about the story of a delegation while these letters were being recited, so the letters carry a weight the audience could feel rather than a puzzle to be solved. Nothing in the verse explains them, and the sources do not agree on a single meaning for them, which is the shape of the verse's instruction, since a chapter that opens without a proposition asks a reader to wait for what the chapter will say, and the verses after this take up a book, a witness and a chain of prophets. The chapter's own opening is also the place where the question of who could bring such a speech is settled, and the answer given there is that an entire community was held back from it, so the letters carry the claim of the book that follows without arguing for it.

**Alif-Lãm-Mĩm, the inability of a people to bring a book like this one, and the story a reciter was told.**

It is said that by listening to these disconnected letters [Alif Lām Mīm] which are contrary to the ordinary customs of human discourse every concept disappears from the hearts whether it be a known written cus tomary or imagined thing and whether it arises from necessity Ḍarūra sensory perception ḥiss or independent reasoning ijtihād. They indicate the inability of the Arabs to bring a Qur’ān like this one despite the fact that it is composed of letters similar to the ones at the beginning of this Sūrah, which also form the parts of their own speech. (Alif. Lam. Mim.) that he said: 'Allah informed us about the story of the delegation of Najran; it is also said that this is an oath by which Allah swore that He is One and that He has neither progeny nor partner. (In the Name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful)(1. Alif-Lam-Mim.)(2. Allah! None has the right to be worshipped but He, the Ever Living, the One Who sustains and protects all that exists.)(3. It is He Who has sent down the Book to you with truth, confirming what came before it. And He sent down the Tawrah and the Injil,)(4. Aforetime, as a guidance to mankind. And He sent down the criterion. Truly, those who disbelieve in the Ayat of Allah, for them there is a severe torment; and Allah is All-Mighty, All-Able of Retribution.)

**The chain of prophets, the agreement of a large number of people, and an age when writing was not in vogue.**

This is the golden chain of prophets from Sayyidna Adam to the Last of the Prophets upto whose time some one hundred and twenty four thousand blessed prophets were born in different periods, speaking different languages, living in different countries. The agreement of a large number of people on a certain principle from the very beginning of humanity may be taken as a natural proof of its reality, if they belong to different times and places, having no means of communicating with each other. They were in an age when, communication through writing was not in vogue, which could make it possible for one prophet to have access to the books and writings of another and might help him to pick up the call of the earlier prophets as his own. The consensus of such a large group of persons consisting of not less than one hundred and twenty four thousand men of different times and places may be enough for establishing the principle, even regardless of their intrinsic trustworthiness. After that, by be-ginning the Surah Al-Baqarah with 1 ‌ (This Book which has no doubt in it), it was pointed out that the prayer made in Su-rah Al-Fatihah for guidance to the straight path has been accepted and Allah Almighty has sent down this Qur'an which provides guidance to the straight path.

**Hearts emptied of what they have imagined, the prayer made so that a people could prevail, and the invitation to look at a power and a wisdom.**

When the hearts are emptied of imagined and known concepts and the innermost selves are purified of customary and familiar things the name Allāh comes to a heart sanctified from everything other [than Him] and to an innermost self purified of every mode [of inquiry] kayf. Since the prayer was made in order that Muslims could confront and prevail over the disbelievers, it was in consonance with that prayer that, in the following Surah 'Al- Imran, the text deals with the modalities of dealing with disbelievers, as well as, with the need to carry out Jihad against them, verbally and physically. Lastly, while referring to the absolute power and wisdom of Allah Almighty, verse 6 invites one's attention to the fact that Allah shapes all men and women in the wombs of their mothers according to His supreme wisdom which has created billions of men and women with clear distinguishable features establishing the identity of each individual distinct from all others.

2.text:
The letters are followed at once by a statement, and the sentence is a testimony before it is a description. "Allah! There is no god worthy of worship except Him, the Ever-Living, All-Sustaining" names the one who is not shared with, then gives two of his qualities, and the sources observe that the order puts the denial and the exception first so that a reader arrives at the attributes through a refusal rather than through an argument. The wording of the first half is about what a person may turn to, and the phrase there is no god is handled as a denial of any other claim on a worshipper rather than a claim about a being who is merely stronger, while the two names that follow are read as the ground on which that refusal stands, a life that has no end and a sustaining of what exists. One source takes the verse as a rational proof of an oneness, on the ground that a thing which cannot bring itself into being and cannot keep itself in being cannot be the one a person bows to, and that the highest point of independence belongs only to what needs nothing. What is brought to the letters beside this treats the whole opening as a claim about speech rather than about a doctrine, so the chapter begins with a testimony and a proof laid side by side, and the verse after this takes up the book in which both are stated.

**The first word at the head of the chapter, and the set of letters a statement is made beside.**

The first word, Alif Lam Mim at the head of the first verse be-longs to the special set of words used by the Qur'an which are words of hidden meaning and are known as Mutashabihat the real meaning of which is a secret between Allah and His Messenger and the details of which appear a little later in the section. In the words (Allah: there is no god but He) which follow immediately, the doctrine of the Oneness of Allah has been put forth as a categorical declaration. Surah Āl-'Imrān was revealed in Al-Madīnah, as evident by the fact that the first eighty-three Ayat in it relate to the delegation from Najran that arrived in Al-Madīnah on the ninth year of Hijrah (632 CE).

**A rational proof of an oneness, and the highest point a thing being worshipped must occupy.**

The first verse of this section presents a rational proof of the Oneness of Allah; the second verse, the reported proof 1, followed by an answer to some doubts nursed by disbelievers towards the later part. In the terminology of Islamic theology, a proof based on rational argument is called rational proof while a proof based on a verse of divine book or on a declaration made by an authority or a report narrated by a trustworthy person is called a reported proof. It, therefore, requires that the one who is being worshipped must occupy the highest point of honour and power and who has to be most perfect from all angles.

**What has no power to come into being, a being that is dependent for its own being, and the bowing a truth asks for.**

Therefore, it is crystal clear that all things in this world which have no power to come into being by themselves, nor can they sustain it - be they idols carved in stone, or water, or trees, or angels and apostles - none of them is worthy of worship. From this it is obvious that anything which cannot sustain its own being, rather is dependent upon somebody else for its very existence, could hardly claim to have any honour or power in its own right. Bowing to the truth required them to bow to the Prophet and to God, and they thought that by surrendering to the Supreme Being and His Prophet they would diminish in stature.

**The One who lives without death or deficiency, the Self-subsistent Creator of the world, and the creation that exists through Him.**

He is the One Who lives perfectly without any death or deficiency. (Allah! There is no God save Him, the Alive) Who dies not and is not evanescent, (the Eternal) the Self-subsistent Who has no beginning. He exists by Himself and is not in need of any of His creation. The creation only exists through Him and is always in need of Him.

3.text:
The chapter moves from a testimony about who God is to a statement about what was sent, and the address is the reason the two belong together. "He has revealed to you O Prophet the Book in truth" gives the book a manner as well as an origin, and the wording of the manner is about truth rather than about beauty or persuasiveness, so the sources read the clause as an answer to a doubt about where the book came from, with the phrase in truth standing against the claim that a man composed it. "confirming what came before it" then places this book among earlier books rather than against them, and the wording is careful, since a confirmation is not a repetition, and the sources discuss what a later book confirms in an earlier one, which is the same question the next clause raises. "as He revealed the Torah and the Gospel" names two of those books and puts them in the same sentence with the same verb, so the Torah and the Gospel are described as things sent down in the manner the verse has just used for this book, with the remark that whenever the Qur'an speaks of the two it means the books themselves rather than the copies a community now has. A reader is left with a chain, a book that testifies to what came before it and a God whose speech is one in its truth, and the verse after this tells what was done with those earlier books and what follows for the people who turn from them. The order within the verse is worth noticing, since the Book of this prophet is named first and the two earlier books are named after it with a repeated verb, and the address that opens the clause is not carried over into that second half, so the Torah and the Gospel are spoken of as things sent to prophets before him rather than as a possession of his own community; a confirmation is therefore given as a relation between two revelations and not as an appeal to their authority, which is how the sources take the phrase in truth, as the quality the later book brings to the earlier ones and not the quality it borrows from them.

**The Book revealed with truth, and the prophet who was told what he had not known.**

(He hath revealed unto thee (Muhammad) the Scripture) He sent you Gabriel with the Scripture (with truth) in order to show truth from falsehood, (confirming) corroborating Allah's divine Oneness (that which was (revealed) before it) of scriptures, (even as He revealed the Torah) in one go to Moses the son of Amran (and the Gospel) in one go to the Jesus the son of Mary. (It is He Who has sent down the Book to you with truth,) means, revealed the Qur'an to you, O Muhammad, in truth, meaning there is no doubt or suspicion that it is revealed from Allah. He has revealed to you, O Prophet, the Qur’ān with true stories and just laws that are in agreement with the previous divine books; and there is no contradiction between all these divine books. He has revealed to you the Book by the truth You did not know O Muḥammad what the Book was nor the story of the lovers.

**The Torah and the Gospel sent down before, and the books that testify to the truth of this one.**

Whenever the Holy Qur'an speaks of the 'Torah and the Injil' it refers to the original books revealed to the prophets Moses and Jesus . (Confirming what came before it) means, from the previous divinely revealed Books, sent to the servants and Prophets of Allah. These Books testify to the truth of the Qur'an, and the Qur'an also testifies to the truth these Books contained, including the news and glad tidings of Muhammad's prophethood and the revelation of the Glorious Qur'an. (And He sent down the Tawrah) to Musa (Musa) son of 'Imran,. That is to say Even though We revealed Our books to the messengers before you We did not omit the remembrance dhikr of you from any book.

**A principle that is not a mere philosophy, the Book sent down to a man who did not know it, and the virtues mentioned with this chapter.**

Briefly stated, it means that the principle of tauhid as de-scribed in the Holy Qur'an is not something peculiar to the Qur'an or the Prophet of Islam. We should also state that we mentioned the virtues of Surah Āl-'Imrān along with the virtues of Surat Al-Baqarah in the beginning of the Tafsir of Surat Al-Baqarah. On the contrary, Allah Almighty has sent Scrip-tures such as the Torah and the Injil, and His prophets, in earlier times.

4.text:
The verse carries the earlier books into the past tense and then turns on the people who refused them. "previously, as a guide for people" attaches to what was revealed before this book, and the wording is about guidance given to people rather than to one community, which is why the sources read the clause as a claim about the reach of the earlier scriptures and not only about their age. "and also revealed the Standard to distinguish between right and wrong" names the fourth thing in the verse, and the wording of a standard is handled by the sources as a cut rather than a hint, a thing that separates a true matter from a false one, so a book that guides is joined to a criterion that decides. "Surely those who reject Allah's revelations will suffer a severe torment" then gives the consequence of refusal, and this with the remark that the verse does not promise a punishment proportionate to the crime but a severe one, which is read against the fact that these people were given a criterion and did not use it. "For Allah is Almighty, capable of punishment" ends the verse on two qualities, a might and an ability to requite, and the sources treat the second as the reason the torment is certain rather than merely possible, since a criterion that decides nothing for anyone would be of no use to a book at all. A reader of the passage so far has been given a book, a confirmation, a Torah, a Gospel, a standard and now a reckoning, and the next verse removes the last place a person can hide, which is the reason the two verses are usually read as one movement rather than as two separate statements about knowledge and about power. Four things are named in this verse and its first half, a Book, a confirmation, a guidance and a Criterion, and the sources keep the third and the fourth apart, since a guidance leads a person who is willing to be led and a Criterion decides a case whether or not anyone attends to it, which is the ground on which the threat that follows is read as the closing of an argument rather than as an outburst, a people having been given the means to tell one matter from another and having declined to use them.

**A guidance for people aforetime, and the Criterion sent down to distinguish a true matter from a false one.**

before that is to say before revealing it the Qur’ān as guidance hudan a circumstantial qualifier meaning hādiyīn ‘guides from error’ to people to those who followed these two Books He uses the word anzala for the revelation of these two and nazzala for that of the Qur’ān for the latter entails repetition whereas the two Books were revealed in one instance; and He revealed the Criterion al-furqān meaning the Scriptures that discriminate between truth and falsehood. (Aforetime) before Muhammad and the Qur'an, (for a guidance to mankind) as a guidance from error to the Children of Israel; (and hath revealed the Criterion (of right and wrong) He revealed the Qur'an to Muhammad in instalments to differentiate the lawful from the unlawful. (And He sent down the criterion) which is the distinction between misguidance, falsehood and deviation on one hand, and guidance, truth and piety on the other hand. He revealed the Criterion to differentiate between truth and falsehood, and between guidance and misguidance. The Quran is not only a genuine book of guidance but also serves as the criterion or standard of right and wrong. Whenever the Holy Qur'an speaks of the 'Torah and the Injil' it refers to the original books revealed to the prophets Moses and Jesus . (Confirming what came before it) means, from the previous divinely revealed Books, sent to the servants and Prophets of Allah.

**Those who reject the signs, the terrible chastisement that awaits them, and the eyes and minds that were granted and refused.**

As for those who disbelieve in God’s signs the Qur’ān or any other revelation for them awaits a terrible chastisement; God is Mighty victorious in His affair so that nothing can prevent Him from effecting His promise and His threat; Lord of Retribution with a severe punishment for those that disobeyed Him the like of which none can do. As for those who disbelieve in God's signs for them awaits a terrible chastisement. [The chastisement] is the ignominy of the veil but they do not perceive [this]. (Lo! those who disbelieve the revelations of Allah) Muhammad and the Qur'an, referring in this context to the delegation of Najran, (theirs will be a heavy doom) in this world and in the next. These are the people to whom their Creator granted minds, but who failed to understand the truth when it came to them in the form of arguments. These are the people to whom God granted eyes, but who failed to see the light (sent by God in the form of this book). (Truly, those who disbelieve in the Ayat of Allah) means they denied, refused and unjustly rejected them,. Now those who, denying the book of the Almighty, refuse to abandon the religion devised by human beings, are deserving of His punishment.

**Mighty and able to requite, the retribution taken from those who reject His messengers, and the sovereignty whose grandeur is invincible.**

(All-Able of Retribution.) from those who reject His Ayat and defy His honorable Messengers and great Prophets. (And Allah is All-Mighty) meaning, His grandeur is invincible and His sovereignty is infinite,. (Allah is Mighty) powerful in His vengeance, (Able to Requite (the wrong) able to carry His vengeance out on them. He is also able to take retribution from those who reject His messengers and go against His instruction. Anyone having imperfect knowledge and limited power can-not be entrusted with this exalted station.

**The guidance sent for man throughout the ages, the final book sent in accordance with a plan, and a religion devised by human beings.**

He has sent guidance for man throughout the ages, including the Torah and the Bible, which were revealed to the former prophets. Ultimately, in accordance with God’s plan, the final book in the form of the Quran was sent down to man. It tells us which is the true religion and which is the religion devised by human beings through misinterpretation. All of these divine books contained guidance and directed people to the best of this world and theAfterlife. On the contrary, Allah Almighty has sent Scrip-tures such as the Torah and the Injil, and His prophets, in earlier times.

**The matter of a pre-eternal choosing that came suddenly, and the books revealed to the messengers before.**

But a matter of pre-eternal choosing came suddenly upon you and cast you into an amazing affair its proof sublime its place of descent and occurrence precious. confirming what was before it that is verifying His promise to you in the books that came through the prophets [ ]. and He revealed the Torah and the Gospel before as guidance to people and He revealed the criterion. That is to say Even though We revealed Our books to the messengers before you We did not omit the remembrance dhikr of you from any book. God is Precious ʿazīz to His friends Lord of Retribution to His enemies. It did not present any new claim which could pose problems for people in its understanding or acceptance. He mentions this Criterion after He has mentioned the three Scriptures so that it encompasses all revealed Scriptures besides these.

5.text:
The verse is one clause long and it closes the space the previous verses had been describing. "Surely nothing on earth or in the heavens is hidden from Allah" takes the two places a person can act in and removes from both of them anything hidden, so the criterion that was sent down to distinguish a true matter from a false one is joined now to a knowledge that has already reached every case, and a reader is left with a decision that is not only offered but watched. The sources read the clause as the ground of what came before it, since a book and a standard would be of no use to a people who could put them aside without being accounted with, and one of them takes the two verses of this opening as a fortification of the doctrine of an oneness, on the ground that the qualities named in them, a life without end, a sustaining of what exists and a knowledge that misses nothing, belong only to a being that needs nothing. Another source puts the point higher, with the statement that a course of action for a person can be determined only by a being who has known the whole of his nature and made it, which makes the verse the reason a law can be trusted rather than merely obeyed. A reader who has been told that a severe torment awaits those who refuse is given here the reason a refusal cannot be kept, and the next verse turns from what is hidden to what is made, in the wombs, PLACEHOLDER_NOT_USED

**The being who knows the whole nature of a person and determines the course he should take.**

It is, therefore, only God who, after placing the nature of man in the perspective of the entire universe, may decree what kind of conduct will guarantee man’s success in this world and the next, for a sound human mentality can only be one which is in harmony with the rest of the world and in complete accord with the vaster system of the cosmos. The right course of action for man can be determined only by a Being who has not only known man from his birth to his death, but also knows what has gone before his birth and what will happen after his death.

**No one presents a need except that it is satisfied, nothing hidden in the heavens or the earth, and the reader eager for the knowledge a book describes.**

As for the elect khuṣūṣ no one presents a need to Him except He satisfies it qāḌīhā and no one has any resource in a calamity except He suffices for it kāfīhā. And He has made this so clear in His Book, that any reader who is eager for knowledge of Him will certainly gain enlightenment from it. Briefly stated, it means that the principle of tauhid as de-scribed in the Holy Qur'an is not something peculiar to the Qur'an or the Prophet of Islam. Nothing no existent thing whatever is hidden in heaven and earth from God on account of His knowledge of universals and particulars. Allah states that He has perfect knowledge in the heavens and earth and that nothing in them is hidden from His watch.

**What is made so clear in the book, the trust a person places in his Maker, and the doctrine the qualities fortify.**

This being so, the only realistic approach for man is to trust in His Maker and accept and follow His guidance wholeheartedly and with full confidence. The last two verses further fortify the doctrine of tauhid on the ground that the attributes of encompassing knowledge and unlimited power are strong proofs of His being the One who possesses the eternal, and all-encompassing knowledge and whose power controls every-thing, and that He is the only One who rightly deserves to be wor-shipped. Truly, nothing is hidden from Allah, in the earth or in the heaven He it is Who shapes you in the wombs as He wills. Anyone having imperfect knowledge and limited power can-not be entrusted with this exalted station.

6.text:
The verse moves from a hidden place to a confession, and the movement is the point. "He is the One Who shapes you in the wombs of your mothers as He wills" is about a making that no one attends, and the wording of the shaping is handled by the sources as a description of particulars rather than a general claim about creation, since the list a reader is given runs to male and female, short and tall, handsome and ugly, which is a set of differences no one chooses. "as He wills" is then read as the whole argument of the clause, because a shape that arrives without the knowledge of the person shaped cannot be traced to his own effort, and one source takes the point further, on the ground that a being who is fashioned in a womb cannot be the one who fashions, which is how the same verse is used against a claim made about the son of Mary: he was created in a womb and shaped in it, so the divinity given to him belongs to the one who shaped him. The confession that follows, "There is no god worthy of worship except Him, the Almighty, All-Wise", is read as the conclusion of that reasoning rather than as a second statement, and the two qualities that close the verse are given their work, a might that nothing resists and a wisdom that arranges the particulars, so the shaping in the wombs is not an arbitrary act but a knowing one. One source puts the same material under two headings, an affirmation of the form of the Creator and an explication of his power over what he made, and the second heading is the one this verse carries, since a shaping in a dark place is a proof of a power rather than a picture of a being; the accounts about a form belong to another discussion, which the same source leaves for its own place.

**He forms you in the wombs as He wills, male and female, short and tall, pretty or ugly.**

He it is Who forms you in the wombs as He will as males or females white black or otherwise. (He it is Who fashioneth you) creates you (in the wombs as pleaseth Him) short or tall, pretty or ugly, male or female, felicitous or damned. He is the One Who creates you in different forms in the wombs of your mothers, as He wills: as male and female, handsome and ugly, black and white. (He it is Who shapes you in the wombs as He wills.) meaning, He creates you in the wombs as He wills, whether male or female, handsome or otherwise, happy or miserable.

**There is no god except Him, the Mighty in his kingdom, the Wise in his actions, the vengeful against whoever does not believe.**

(There is no God) there is no fashioner or creator (save Him, the Almighty) Who is vengeful against whoever does not believe in Him, (the Wise) in creating what is in wombs. There is no god except Him the Mighty in His Kingdom the Wise in His actions. (La ilaha illa Huwa (none has the right to be worshipped but He), the Almighty, the All-Wise.) meaning, He is the Creator and thus is the only deity worthy of worship, without partners, and His is the perfect might, wisdom and decision.

**The son of Mary was created in a womb and shaped in it, so how could he be the one who shaped him.**

This Ayah refers to the fact that 'Isa, son of Mary, is a created servant, just as Allah created the rest of mankind. Allah created 'Isa in the womb (of his mother) and shaped him as He willed. Therefore, how could 'Isa be divine, as the Christians, may Allah's curses descend on them, claim? 'Isa was created in the womb and his creation changed from stage to stage, just as Allah said,.

**Affirming the form of the Creator and expounding a power over creation, with investigation and reflection set aside.**

Talk of this has two sides: the affirmation of the form of the Creator, and the explication of His power over creatures and favor toward them through predetermination and form-giving. As for affirming the form of the Creator, in a sound report MuṣṬafā said, "God created Adam in His form, and his height was sixty cubits. Only God can truly tell us what He is in His Being and in His attributes. They say that in this report the pronoun refers to God, that investigation, reflection, and interpretation are not allowed, and that fancying similarity is an error, for the Real is without peer in all attributes. " Anas also said, "Among the favors God will bestow on Adam on the Day of Resurrection is that He will say, 'Did I not bestow upon you My form?

7.text:
The verse divides the Book in two and then divides its readers in two, and the sources keep those two divisions tied together, since a reader's posture toward an elusive verse tells a person more about him than the verse does. "He is the One Who has revealed to you O Prophet the Book" repeats the opening of the verse before it, so the discussion that follows is placed inside a claim about origin, and the wording of the Book is read by one source as covering the whole Qur'an rather than a part of it, which is the reason the two kinds of verses are described as belonging to one book and not as two books kept apart. "of which some verses are precise" gives the first kind, and the word for precise is handled as a matter of a reader's competence rather than of a hidden property, a verse being clear to a person who knows the rules of the language and the terms in use, while "they are the foundation of the Book" is glossed as the leading theme, the part on which the rest stands. "while others are elusive" gives the second kind, and the sources are careful here, since elusiveness is described as a property of a hearer's capacity rather than of the speech, one of them explaining that a phrase about a hand or a face belongs to the known human world and is therefore expressed in an everyday style, while what falls outside that world cannot be put in a form the senses would complete. "Those with deviant hearts follow the elusive verses seeking to spread doubt through their false interpretations" is read against a particular set of people in the accounts brought to the verse, and the following clause, "but none grasps their full meaning except Allah", is taken by most of the sources as an end to the discussion, a statement that the inner meaning of such verses is not a piece of knowledge a person may acquire. "As for those well-grounded in knowledge, they say, We believe in this Quran—it is all from our Lord" is then held up as the alternative, and the wording of the prayer is worth noting, since the belief given there is a single act directed at the whole, with no division between what a reader understands and what he does not. "But none will be mindful of this except people of reason" closes the verse on a definition of the audience, and the sources take the two halves of the verse as a test, an elusive verse being the instrument by which a heart is known.

**The Book revealed, the clear verses, and the Mother of the Book.**

He it is Who revealed to you the Book wherein are verses that are clear lucid in proof forming the Mother Book the original basis for rulings and others allegorical whose meanings are not known such as the opening verses of some sūras. (He it is Who hath revealed unto thee (Muhammad) the Scripture) who sent you Gabriel with the Scripture (wherein are clear revelations) expositing the lawful and unlawful which are not abrogated and which are acted upon. O Prophet, He is the One Who revealed to you the Qur’ān, which contains verses with clear and unambiguous meaning, and these represent the majority of the Book and are the reference point when there is disagreement. He it is who has sent down upon thee the Book, wherein are firm verses, which are the mother of the Book, and others ambiguous. Allah Almighty has called the first kind of verses, that is, the Muhkamat Umm al-Kitab ' (which has been translated literally as 'mother verses') meaning thereby that such verses are the very root and essence of all teachings, and the meanings and explanations of which are free of doubt or ambiguity.

**Two kinds of subjects, one from the known human world and one from what lies beyond it.**

There are two kinds of subjects dealt with in the Quran, one pertaining to the known human world, like historical events, signs from the universe and commandments for worldly life; the other pertaining to unseen matters which are not comprehensible by man in this life, for instance, God’s attributes, and the states of Heaven and Hell, etc. The first are clear revelations, quite precise in their meaning, since they have been couched in a direct style. The second relate to the unknown world (for man) and cannot, therefore, be expressed in everyday language. For instance, if we say, ‘man’s hand’, this is an example of the expression of a fact, but if we say, ‘God’s hand’, this is an example of an allegory. Those who do not understand this difference fall into the error of interpreting allegorical verses quite literally.

**Those whose hearts incline away follow what is elusive, and the doubt their reading is meant to produce.**

As for those in whose hearts is deviation inclination away from truth they follow the allegorical part desiring sedition among the ignorant of them throwing them into specious arguments and confusion and desiring its interpretation its explanation and none knows its interpretation its explanation save God Him alone. Those who seek other than the truth leave the clear verses and focus on the unclear ones, trying to create doubts and mislead people, and interpret them to suit their corrupt views. (But those) the Jews Ka'b Ibn al-Ashraf, Huyayy Ibn Akhtab and Judayy Ibn Akhtab (in whose hearts is doubt) scepticism, opposition and deviance from guidance (pursue, forsooth, that which is allegorical seeking) in the Qur'an ((to cause) dissension) pursuing disbelief, ascribing partners to Allah, and holding fast to the error they are in (by seeking to explain it) to determine the future of this nation so that dominion reverts back to them. Now, if someone closes his eyes towards all these verses which have an established meaning and unnecessarily coils with the expressions, (the Word of Allah) and ‌ (a spirit from Him) and their likes from the category of Mutashabihat (verses whose definite meanings cannot be ascertained) and starts deducing from them meanings which are against the Muhkamat of Qur'an and other consistent statements, then, that would be a simple case of going astray and being ob-stinate.

**The people firmly grounded in knowledge, whose faith is given to the whole of the Book.**

And those firmly rooted established and capable in knowledge al-rāsikhūna fī’l-‘ilm is the subject the predicate of which is what follows say ‘We believe in it the allegorical part that it is from God and we do not know its meaning; all of the clear and the allegorical is from our Lord’; yet none remembers yadhdhakkar the initial tā’ of yatadhakkar has been assimilated with the dhāl that is none is admonished but people of pith possessors of intellect who when they see those following that allegorical part only also say. (And those who are of sound instruction) those who have a sound grasp of the knowledge of the Torah: 'Abdullah Ibn Salam and his fellow companions (say: We believe therein) in the Qur'an; (the whole is from our Lord) Allah has revealed both those verses which are clear and those which are ambiguous; (but only men of understanding) who have sound minds such as 'Abdullah Ibn Salam and his fellow companions (really heed) take admonition from the simile of the Qur'an. The weightier position is that the reference here is to ahl al-sunnah wa al jama’ ah the main body of Muslims who give credence only to that interpretation and explanation of the Holy Qur'an and Sunnah which has been authentically reported from the blessed Companions the righteous generations following them and upon which there is the consensus of the Muslim community, and who believe that the Muhhamat (verses of established meaning) of Qur'an are its axis and centre, and who, humbly confessing their limitations of knowledge and insight, leave to Allah the real meanings of Mutashabihat which are beyond their compre-hension and conceptualization. Those who are firm in knowledge say, ‘We have faith in the entire Qur’ān because it is all from Allah’.

**A delegation that came to the Prophet and the doubts they raised about two words used for the son of Mary.**

Once a group of Christians came to the Holy Prophet and started talking about religion. The Holy Prophet refuted their doctrine of Trinity in details and proved the Oneness of Allah with reference to the eternal existence, the perfect power, the all encompassing knowledge; and the most unique creativity of Allah Almighty who had to be One and indivisible. Jesus Christ has been called 'Ruhullah ' (the Spirit of Allah) or 'Kalimatullah ' (the Word of Allah), which according to them led to prove that Sayyidna Isa had a share in the divinity of Allah. Through this verse, Allah Almighty has put an end to these doubts by saying that such expressions are in the category of Mutashabihat where the outward meaning is not intended; they are, rather, a secret between Allah and His Messenger, the reality of which cannot become manifest to others for whom it is not even appropriate to go about determining the possible meanings of these words. One has to have faith in them by believing that whatever Allah Almighty has elected to mean through them is the truth.

**The principle the verse settles, the position a reader may not take, and the two divisions of the Book.**

Mutashabihat right there in the beginning, pointed out towards a general principle which, if understood, could eradicate many doubts and disputes. The principle is that the Holy Qur'an has two kinds of verses; one is known as the Muhkamat (of established meaning) and the other as the Mutashabihat (whose definite meanings are unknown). Muhkamat is the name of verses the meaning of which is open and clear to one who knows the rules of Arabic grammar fairly well. These are the two great divisions of the Qur'an, one apparent and clear, the other abstruse and difficult. The ap parent belongs to the majesty of the Shariah, and the difficult belongs to the beauty of the Haqiqah.

8.text:
The verse hands the reader the words of the people described in the verse before it, and the shift is the reason the prayer is read as instruction rather than as decoration. "They say, Our Lord! Do not let our hearts deviate after you have guided us" asks for the keeping of a thing already given, and the wording of a deviation is handled by the sources with the same care the previous verse used, since a heart that turns away after guidance is the condition the elusive verses expose, so the prayer is a refusal of the posture described there rather than a general petition. One account brought to this wording gives the reason a person asks another for what only God can keep, a heart being described as lying between the two fingers of the Merciful, turning where it is turned, and the sources read the prayer as the admission that steadiness is not a possession of the one who is steady, which is why the asking follows the guidance instead of preceding it. "Grant us Your mercy" then asks for more than the keeping of a state, since the clause is glossed as a request for the wisdom that lets a person know his own place and be content with it, and the wording of a mercy is expanded by one source into what guides a heart and protects it from misguidance, which is the same thing asked in the first clause with a different name. "You are indeed the Giver of all bounties" ends the prayer on the ground of the asking, and the sources take the closing as the reason the verse is placed here, a people who have been guided having been given, in this verse, the form of asking for what they cannot secure for themselves.

**Our Lord, do not cause our hearts to deviate after You have guided us, in their desire to interpret.**

Our Lord do not cause our hearts to deviate do not cause them to incline away from the truth in their desire to interpret it such as is inappropriate for us — as You caused the hearts of those others to deviate — after You have guided us after You have shown us the way to it; and give us mercy from You as a strengthening; You are the Bestower. (Cause not our hearts to stray) do not make our hearts deviate from Your Religion (after Thou hast guided us) to Your Religion, (and bestow upon us mercy from Thy Presence) make us firm in holding to Your religion. The ones firm in knowledge say, ‘O Lord, do not let our hearts move away from the truth after you have shown it to us. Our Lord, let not our hearts stray after Thou hast guided us, and give us mercy from Thee.

**There is no heart but that it is between the two fingers of the Merciful, and a heart tilts to what it is made for.**

This is just as it was said in a hadith of the Holy Prophet There is no heart which is not there in between the two of Allah's fingers - He makes it firm on the truth as long as He wills, and turns it away from the truth when He wills. When Allah intends to guide someone, He makes his heart tilt towards what is good and right; and when He decides to let someone go astray, He turns his heart away from the straight path. (Our Lord! Let not our hearts deviate (from the truth) after You have guided us.) meaning, "Do not deviate our hearts from the guidance after You allowed them to acquire it. The present verse mentions yet another excellence of theirs - that they pray for steadfastness on the right path, not for any worldly gains, but for salvation in the life-to-come.

**The path of the intellect is slippery, so a man is given wisdom to recognize his place and be content.**

The correct academic and intellectual stand regarding the allegorical part of the Quran is for man to acknowledge his limitations. One should be content to have an abstract understanding of the things which cannot be grasped precisely by the senses. When, due to his imperfect sensory perception, man cannot have a total understanding of those realities, the practical approach should be not to make any attempt to determine the precise meaning in these matters. He should pray to God to grant him such wisdom as will enable him to recognize his place and be content to repose his faith in those realities, without knowing all of their details. The path of the intellect may be a slippery one, where the intellectual may slip and fall in failing to see things in their right perspective.

**Grant us mercy from You, for You alone are the Bestower, and a heart made limpid at the remembrance of the Real.**

(Lo! Thou, only Thou art the Bestower) to the believers before us; it is also said that this means: Give us, from Your vast mercy, that which will guide our hearts and protect us from misguidance. When they were truthful in the beauty of asking for help, He assisted them with the lights of suf ficiency. When the heart is limpid, the present moment empty, and the tongue flowing with the Real's remembrance, the arrow of supplication inevitably reaches the target of response. "O God, keep our hearts far from confusion and straying and make us firm on the carpet of service with the stipulation of the Sunnah.

9.text:
The prayer asked in the verse before this is continued with a second clause, and the second clause is about a Day rather than about a heart. "Our Lord! You will certainly gather all humanity for the promised Day, about which there is no doubt" puts the asking inside a claim about what will happen to everyone, and the wording of the gathering is handled by the sources as the point of the whole prayer, since a people who ask to be kept steady are asking on the assumption that a settling of accounts follows, with the remark that the concern of these speakers is with the matter of the Hereafter rather than with what they have lost in this world. The phrase about which there is no doubt is read against the people who were told about the Day in their own scripture, and one source makes the gathering a present affair as well as a future one, with a gathering of the lovers now and a gathering of all later, which is the way the same wording is used to describe an unveiling rather than a summons to a place. "Surely Allah does not break His promise" gives the ground of the whole, and the sources take the clause as the reason the previous verse's request for mercy is confident, a promise having been given and a gathering having been named, with material considerations ceasing to matter when the veil is rent. Two accounts are brought to this wording in which the Prophet is heard reciting at a reckoning, and they place the verse in a practice rather than in an argument, since the line is given as something spoken aloud for a people being warned, The sources also dwell on a small detail of the wording, since the closing of the verse changes who is being spoken to, a petition addressed to God being followed by a statement about him in the third person, and one source leaves open which of the two readings the verse carries, whether the speakers end with a confession or the confession is spoken back to them. The phrase about which there is no doubt is taken in the same way, as a refusal of a hesitation a hearer might bring to the report rather than as a description of the Day, since a Day that arrives with no doubt about it is a thing already settled and only awaiting its time, which is a fitting end for a verse whose subject is an assembly no one is excused from attending.

**You will gather all humanity for a Day about which there is no doubt, a calling back and a holding to account.**

Our Lord You shall gather mankind for a day that is on a day of which there is no doubt no uncertainty that is the Day of Resurrection when You will requite them for their deeds as You had promised; verily God will not fail the tryst His promise of the Upraising there is a shift of address here from the second to the third person and these last words could constitute God’s speech. Our Lord, You are going to call all people back to You: to hold them to account on a day in which there is no doubt. (it is Thou Who gatherest mankind together) after they die (to a Day) on a day (of which there is no doubt. Lo! Allah faileth not to keep the tryst) resurrection after death, the reckoning, the Bridge over hell, the Scale, Paradise and hell.

**The gathering of the lovers on the carpet of approach, and the gathering of all on the Day of the tryst.**

Today is the gathering of the lovers on the carpet of approach iqtirāb and tomorrow will be the gathering of all in the place of reward thawāb and punishment ʿiqāb. Today is the gathering of innermost selves asrār for the unveiling of [divine] Majesty jalāl and Beauty jamāl and tomor row will be the gathering of human beings abshār to witness the terrors ahwāl and endure what has been told of these states aḥwāl. The purpose of their supplication in this way is to show that their concern is with the matter of the Hereafter and for this reason they ask God for adherence to the path of guidance in order to attain its reward.

**The verse recited aloud, a warning to beware of those pursuing what is elusive, and a fear for a community when the Book is opened.**

The two Shaykhs Bukhārī and Muslim reported that ‘Ā’isha may God be pleased with her said ‘The Messenger of God s recited this verse It is He Who revealed to you the Book wherein are verses clear to the end of the verse and said “When you see those pursuing the allegorical parts know that these are the ones God refers to in this verse so beware of them” ’. Al-Tabarānī reported in his al-Kabīr that Abū Mūsā al-Ash‘arī heard the Prophet s say ‘I fear nothing for my community except three faults’ and he mentioned that one of these would be when the Book is opened in front of them and the believer will desire to interpret it and yet none knows its interpretation save God; and those firmly rooted in knowledge say ‘We believe in it all is from our Lord; yet none remembers but people of pith’ Q. 37 end of the hadīth.

**The Day of Judgement when all issues are settled between a person and God, and the Day of Return when what they disputed is decided.**

But all the material considerations that appear important today will cease to matter on the Day of Judgement. The Day the veil of Doomsday is rent asunder, and all issues are to be settled between man and God, all worldly things will become insignificant—as if they had never existed. ("Our Lord! Verily, it is You Who will gather mankind together on the Day about which there is no doubt") meaning, they say in their supplication: You will gather Your creation on the Day of Return, judge between them and decide over what they disputed about. Thereafter, You will reward or punish each according to the deeds they did in this life.

**Ta'wil with two meanings in the Book, the true reality of things and what they turn out to be on the Day of Resurrection.**

Ta'wil has two meanings in the Qur'an, the true reality of things, and what they will turn out to be. (Await they just for it's Ta'wil? On the Day (Day of Resurrection) it's Ta'wil is finally fulfillled.)(7:53) refers to the true reality of Resurrection that they were told about. If this is the meaning desired in the Ayah above , then pausing after reciting Allah's Name is warranted, because only Allah knows the true reality of things. (say: "We believe in it") If the word Ta'wil means the second meaning, that is, explaining and describing, such as what Allah said,.

10.text:
The verse takes the two things a person counts as a defence and removes their use. "Indeed, neither the wealth nor children of the disbelievers will be of any benefit to them against Allah" is read by the sources with the words against Allah attached to what is feared rather than to God himself, one of them glossing the phrase as protection against a chastisement, since no one is being told that a man cannot buy or bequeath anything. The wording of a benefit is then handled as a question of time, one source extends it to both horizons, the wealth and the children failing to protect in this world or in the next, and another taking the clause to mean that possessions do not even take away the need a person has, which is a smaller claim and the more telling of the two. "and they will be the fuel for the Fire" gives the other half, and the sources attend to a single letter in the word for fuel, a reading in which the disbelievers are what the fire is fuelled by rather than the wood put into it, which is how the clause is turned from an image into an account of what a person becomes. The turn one commentary takes here is the reason the verse is not read as a rebuke of possession as such: the same possessions are useful to the faithful once what is due on them has been carried out, and a measure of sufficiency that leaves a person free for worship is itself worship, being the supplies for a road that is part of the road. The commentary then draws the line at excess, since passing beyond the measure is what makes a thing a cause of rebellion, and it carries the discussion down to the body, the light of a heart coming from a lamp whose root is a divine bestowal and its material from the acts of the body, which come in turn from food, drink and clothing — so a Prophet's prayer for a family's food at the measure of sufficiency belongs in the same verse as the warning about riches.

**Neither their riches nor their children will avail them or protect them against a chastisement.**

As for the disbelievers neither their riches nor their children will avail will protect them against God that is against His chastisement; those — they shall be fuel for the Fire they shall constitute what the Fire will be fuelled by read waqūd as opposed to wuqūd ‘fuel’. ((On that day) neither the riches) the abundance of riches (nor the progeny) nor the abundance of progeny (of those who disbelieve) i.e. The wealth and children of the disbelievers in Allah and His Messenger will not protect them from Allah’s punishment in this world nor in the Afterlife. As for the unbelievers, their possessions will not take away their need for God, neither their children, and it is they who will be fuel for the Fire. The denier appears to be influential in this world, but is, in fact, totally powerless, because his strength is nothing but a temporary delusion.

**They will be the fuel with which Hell is lit, what is useless at the resurrection, and what is useful to the faithful once its due is carried out.**

Such disbelievers will be the fuel with which Hell will be lit on the Day of Resurrection. He is saying, "Tomorrow at the res urrection possessions and children will be useless to the unbelievers and will not profit them. What a majestic God, generous, lovingly kind, who promises the faithful in the midst of warning the unbelievers and who caresses these while blaming those! " In other words, they will be useful to the faithful whenever they have carried out what is rightfully due to them, making them the snare of their own religion and seeking through them their endless felicity.

**The measure of sufficiency that is itself worship, and the road supplies that become a cause of rebellion.**

" When the measure of sufficiency is for the leisure to worship, then it itself is nothing but worship, for it is the supplies for the road, and the road supplies are also part of the road. But, one must not pass beyond the measure of sufficiency, for then these will become the cause of rebellion, just as He says: He is saying, "In that of this world which He has given you, bring the next world to hand!

**The light of a heart, its material from the deeds of the body, the root of its lamp in a divine bestowal, and the food of a family asked of God in prayer.**

The light of the heart comes from the lamp of tawḤīd, and the root of this lamp is the divine bestowal. As for its material, that comes from the deeds and obedient acts of the body. Obedient acts come from the strength of the soul, and the soul's strength comes from food, drink, and clothing. This is why God's Messenger supplicated, "Lord God, make the food of Muhammad's family in the measure of sufficiency!

11.text:
The verse sets one people against another, and the sources are precise about what the likeness covers. "Their fate will be like that of the people of Pharaoh and those before them" is glossed on the word for a way of acting, one account carrying that gloss back to a companion of the Prophet, so the comparison is first a comparison of conduct and only then of outcomes, which is why the phrase that follows, "they all rejected Our signs", is read as the shared part of the two stories rather than the punishment. "so Allah seized them for their sins" is then handled as the second half of the likeness, and the sources read the sequence carefully, a persistent insolence drawing a retribution that follows its own measure, with one account putting the point as a door found blocked and a regret arriving too late to be accepted. The material brought to this verse also fixes a date, since the day of drowning is joined to the day of Badr, which is how the verse is used to read the earlier clauses about riches and children as a statement about what happened rather than a general prediction, and one source takes the two verses before this as an introduction to a warning about an encounter that is coming, so the likeness is doing the work of an argument: a people who have been given a criterion and refused it are placed in a series. "And Allah is severe in punishment" closes the verse on a quality, and the sources attach it to what precedes rather than to a threat on its own, a might that prevails over all things and receives the humility of everything in it, so that the severity named here is the same quality the beginning of the chapter put beside a life without end, while the person who carries the claim looks powerless in the world that is measuring power. The gloss on the word for a way of acting is given in four terms in one source, a practice, a conduct, a tradition and a habit, and the variety is the point, since a habit is a thing a people keep doing rather than a thing that happens to them, which is why the likeness to the people of Pharaoh is read as an instruction about conduct and not as a prediction a reader could sit through. The closing quality receives the same treatment, the severity being glossed as a torment that is painful, the two words standing for an ending rather than for a mood, and another account attaches the severity to the denial of the signs, so that the verse's last clause answers its middle clause rather than its first. The account of the worldly scale in the same block belongs here as well, since the assets of comfort and grandeur are set against a caravan of truth whose joining costs a person his own social circle, and the material considerations that decide a man's conduct today are given a duration, lasting only while dealings are between people and ceasing when the reckoning opens, which is how the likeness is read as a warning about a weighing done elsewhere.

**Their way is as the way of the folk of Pharaoh and the communities before them, who denied the signs.**

Their way is as the way as the habit of Pharaoh’s folk and the communities of people before them such as ‘Ād and Thamūd who denied Our signs; God seized them He destroyed them for their sins this statement explains the previous one; God is severe in retribution. Verily, those who disbelieve, neither their properties nor their offspring will avail them whatsoever against Allah; and it is they who will be fuel of the Fire Like the behavior of the people of Fir'awn and those before them; they belied Our Ayat.

**Like the behaviour of the people of Pharaoh: the end the nations met, the messengers and the books denied, and what they were granted not saving them.**

(Like the Da'b of the people of Fira'wn.) Ad-Dahhak said that Ibn 'Abbas said that the Ayah means, "Like the behavior of the people of Fir'awn. This is the same end the people of Fir'awn and the previous nations met, those who rejected the Messengers, the Ayat, and proofs of Allah that they were sent with. (Verily, those who disbelieve) meaning, disbelieved in Allah's Ayat, denied His Messengers, defied His Books and did not benefit from His revelation to His Prophets,. (Neither their properties nor their offspring will avail them whatsoever against Allah; and it is they who will be fuel of the Fire.) meaning, they will be the wood with which the Fire is kindled and fed. Allah does what He wills and prevails over all things, it is He to Whom everything is humbled and there is no deity worthy of worship, nor any Lord except Him. (So let not their wealth nor their children amaze you; in reality Allah's plan is to punish them with these things in the life of this world, and that their souls shall depart while they are disbelievers.)[9:55], and,. The missionary in this world appears to be powerless, but in reality, he is powerful, because God is backing him.

**What is done with them on the Day of Badr as on the day of drowning, and a text turning from words to an encounter.**

And We (Allah) shall do with them on the Day of Badr as We did with the people of Moses on the day of drowning, (and those who were before them) before the people of Moses, (they disbelieved Our revelations) they disbelieved in the Scripture and Messenger We sent to them (and so Allah seized them) destroyed them (for their sins) because of their denial. Allah says here: your people have done with you-by giving you the lie and abusing you-as the people of Moses did with him: they gave him the lie and abused him. As a result, Allah punished them for their sins – their wealth and children did not benefit them. The text now shifts from the verbal confrontation with disbelievers on the warnings about the coming physical encounter as pointed out in verse 12 - 'You shall soon be overcome (by Muslims) ' while the verses earlier (10 and 11) serve as the introduction.

**They persisted in their insolence, and the door was found blocked when the regret came.**

They persisted in insolence according to their way sunna and We brought them retribution according to Our way sunna. They would not stop their persistent [insolence] fa-lā ʿan al-iṣrār aqlaʿū and did not strive to do anything good wa-lā fī l-mabārri Ṭamiʿū. By my life they are those who suffered regret and distress at what they put forward but by that time they found the door blocked wajadū l-bāba masdūdan and their repentance rejected wa-l-nadama ʿalayhim mardūdan. On the one hand, there are all the assets of worldly comfort and grandeur, while, on the other hand, there is the caravan of truth, having no foothold in society, and no worldly interests attached to it. In such a situation, joining the caravan of truth amounts to detachment from the social circle and depriving oneself of all material benefits. But all the material considerations that appear important today will cease to matter on the Day of Judgement. Their importance will last only so long as dealings are between man and man.

**A way of acting explained as practice, conduct, tradition and habit, a punishment whose torment is painful, and a wealth and an offspring that will not benefit.**

Other scholars said that the Ayah means, "Like the practice, conduct, likeness of the people of Fir'awn. " These meanings are all plausible, for the Da'b means practice, behavior, tradition and habit. (And Allah is severe in punishment.) meaning, His punishment is severe and His torment is painful. The Ayah indicates that the disbelievers will not benefit from their wealth or offspring.

12.text:
The verse is a message to be delivered, and the occasion the sources give it explains the sharpness of the wording. "O Prophet! Tell the disbelievers" is addressed to a group the accounts place in Madīnah after the day of Badr, and the material brought to the verse preserves a demand made of them to enter Islam, their answer to it, and the revelation that follows the answer, so the clause is not a proclamation to an abstraction but a reply to a sentence spoken to the Prophet. Their words are given in full in one account, a warning not to be deceived by a victory over men with no knowledge of warfare, and in another the assembly is gathered and told to embrace Islam before what befell Quraysh befalls them, with the ground of the demand being what their own scripture and their covenant already carried. "Soon you will be overpowered and driven to Hell" is then read by the sources across two horizons, one of them taking the overcoming as killing, captivity and the tax taken in this world and the mustering as the next, and a second reading attaches the first clause to the day of Badr itself; one source raises the obvious objection, that disbelievers are not visibly overcome in every place and every age, and answers it by limiting the addressees to the disbelievers and the Jews of that particular time, so the verse is a prediction with a scope rather than a law of history. "what an evil place to rest" closes it, and one commentary on the inner sense reads the closing as a description of a present condition, the pain of a separation that their insight has become too dimmed to feel, which is the reason the verse's two halves, an overcoming here and a mustering there, are usually taken as one announcement rather than as two punishments.

**Say to those who disbelieve: you shall be overcome and gathered unto Hell, an evil resting place, and a promise not universal in its scope.**

O Messenger, say to those who disbelieve, no matter what their religion, ‘The believers will defeat you and you will die as disbelievers. (Ye shall be overcome) You shall be killed on the Day of Badr (and gathered unto hell) on the Day of Judgement, (an evil resting place) an evil place and outcome. Some readers of verse 12: ‌ just cited, above may have some doubt about disbelievers being overcome because this is not the case with all disbelievers of the world. But, this doubt is unfounded as the disbelievers referred to here are the disbelievers and Jews of that particular time - from among whom, the pagans were overcome when killed or taken prisoners, and the Jews were overcome through killing or imprisonment as well as through Jizya and extradition. Therefore, this 'overcoming' of disbelievers mentioned in the verse simply does not refer to disbelievers universally.

**The day of Badr and the Jews of Madīnah: a banner not to be defeated, a treaty dissolved, and an embassy riding to Makkah.**

When Allah defeated the idolaters on the day of Badr, the Jews of Medina said: 'By Allah, this is the unlettered Prophet who was announced to us by Moses and whose attribute and description we find in our Scriptures and about whom it is also mentioned that his banner will not be defeated'. Meanwhile, they had a treaty with the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, which was supposed to last up to a certain period. They dissolved that treaty and Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf set off, along with sixty riders, to meet the people of Makkah, Abu Sufyan and his companions. They said: 'Our word shall be one!' When they went back to Medina, Allah, exalted is He, revealed the above verse about them . Allah, exalted is He, then revealed (Say (O Muhammad) unto those who disbelieve) i.e. the Jews (Ye shall be overcome) you shall be defeated (and gathered unto Hell) in the Afterlife ; this is the narration of 'Ikrimah and Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas.

**The congregation assembled after the return, an injunction to embrace Islam, and the answer that was not to be deceived.**

When the Prophet s enjoined the Jews to enter into Islam after his return from Badr they said ‘Do not fool yourself just because you killed a few men of Quraysh inexperienced and knowing nothing about fighting’ whereupon the following was revealed Say O Muhammad to the disbelievers from among the Jews ‘You shall be vanquished sa-tughlabūn or read sa-yughlabūn ‘they shall be vanquished’ in this world through being killed or taken captive and made to pay the jizya which actually took place and mustered read in both ways wa-tuhsharūna ‘you will be mustered’ or wa-yuhsharūna ‘they will be mustered’ in the Hereafter to Hell which you shall enter — an evil cradling!’ an evil resting place. When the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, defeated the Quraysh at Badr and then went back to Medina, he gathered the Jews and said: 'O congregation of Jews! Beware lest Allah inflicts on you the like of that which he has inflicted on Quraysh on the day of Badr; embrace Islam before that which has befallen them befalls you. This you find it mentioned in your Scripture as well as in Allah's covenant with you'. Be not deluded because you have defeated inexperienced people who have no knowledge of warfare. By Allah, if we were to fight, you will realize that we are the real thing'.

**No delight in the present life, the severity of a burning in the next, and a call of Truth that appears to people of no value.**

He informed them that the speech of the Real will elude them in the future ājil and they will have no delight in living in the present #703;ājil. In the hereafter what they will encounter will be from the severity of the punishment by burning ḥurqa. What [already] afflicts them in this world is absence and separation furqa from God but their faculties of insight have become weak and they do not perceive the pain of [that] punishment. When the call of Truth goes out, it appears to people to be of no value.

**A threat of defeat and an encouragement to learn a lesson from the battle, the addressees named, and a proof that a religion will prevail.**

Threatening the Jews With Defeat and Encouraging Them to Learn a Lesson From the Battle of Badr. (There has already been a sign for you) meaning, O Jews, who said what you said! You have an Ayah, meaning proof, that Allah will make His religion prevail, award victory to His Messenger, make His Word apparent and His religion the highest. "You will be defeated and gathered together to Hell, and worst indeed is that place of rest.

13.text:
The verse returns to a battlefield and asks the reader to look at it as evidence. "Indeed, there was a sign for you in the two armies that met in battle" is fixed by the sources to Badr, and the wording of a sign is read as confirmation of a prophethood rather than as a memorial of a victory, one account remarking that a verb in the clause sets the statement apart from what went before it, so the verse is being introduced as an example already given and not as a promise still awaited. "one fighting for the cause of Allah and the other in denial" is then expanded into figures, the smaller group at three hundred and thirteen men, most of them on foot, with two horses, six pieces of armour and eight swords, the other at nine hundred and fifty or about a thousand with seven hundred camels, and the sources treat the numbers as part of the argument, since the disproportion is what makes the outcome a sign. "The believers saw their enemy twice their number" is handled as the strangest clause in the verse, and one source takes it in two directions, each group seeing the other as twice its own numbers at one time and as fewer at another, with the awe that came over one side and the fervour that came over the other being the point of the doubling: a sighting that steadies the believers and unsettles their opponents is a thing done for them, not a mistake in their eyes. "But Allah supports with His victory whoever He wills" states the cause, and the closing "Surely in this is a lesson for people of insight" is glossed as a lesson for those who have eyes in religion, a phrase one source reads as a description of believers and another as a description of the people who stood there and saw it, which is the difference between a sign for a reader of the verse and a sign for a witness of it.

**A sign in two hosts that met on the Day of Badr, one company fighting in the way of God, three hundred and thirteen against almost a thousand.**

There has already been a sign an example the verb qad kāna ‘there has been’ is used to separate the statement to follow from the previous one for you in two hosts two parties that met one another in battle on the day of Badr; one company fighting in the way of God in obedience to Him namely the Prophet and his Companions who numbered three hundred and thirteen men most of them on foot with two horses six plates of armour and eight swords; and another unbelieving; they the disbelievers numbering almost a thousand saw them the Muslims twice the like of them that is more numerous than themselves as the eye sees in manifest vision witnessing; and God granted them victory despite their fewer number; for God confirms He strengthens with His help whom He will granting him victory. (There was a token) a sign confirming the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ (for you) O people of Makkah (in two hosts) in two groups: that of Muhammad and that of Abu Sufyan (which met) on the Day of Badr: There has already been a sign for you in two hosts that met; one com pany fighting in the way of God; and another unbelieving; they saw them twice the like of them; for God confirms with His help whom He will.

**Three hundred and thirteen men with two horses, six armours and eight swords, against a host of nine hundred and fifty and seven hundred camels.**

This verse refers to the Battle of Badr in which the disbelievers had about 1000 men, 700 camels and 100 horses, while the Muslim mujahidin were just over 300, having a total of 70 camels, 2 horses, 6 armours and 8 swords. Muhammad and his Companions who were 313 men, (and another disbelieving) and another group of disbelievers in Allah and the Messenger: Abu Sufyan and his army which consisted of 950 men, (whom they saw) they saw themselves (as twice their number) as twice the number as that of the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ (clearly, with their very eyes). One group was made up of believers, and this was the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions: they were fighting for Allah’s sake and in order to raise His Word against the word of those who disbelieve. The other group consisted of the disbelievers of Makkah, who had come out in pride and for show.

**Each combating group saw the other as twice its own numbers, one struck with awe and the other turning to God more fervently.**

The encounter was certainly strange as each combating group saw the opponent being twice its own numbers. The sighting of so many Muslims inspired awe in the hearts of the disbelievers, while Muslims who saw the disbelievers as twice of them turned to Allah more fervently. They had hopes of Allah's help, and ultimate victory, because they had placed their total trust in Allah, were steadfast and sincerely believed in the promise of Allah revealed to them in the following words: If the actual number of disbelievers which was three times more than their own were to be realized by Muslims, they may have been overawed. This state of sighting the numbers of the other group as twice its own was at a particular time. At another time each of the two combating groups felt the other one as low in numbers, as it would appear later in Surah al-Anfal.

**Herein is a lesson for those who have eyes concerning religion, many made to appear few and few made to appear many.**

Surely in that which is mentioned is a lesson for people of vision those who are discerning so will you not be warned by this and become believers? When God wants an affair to be accomplished He makes many appear to be few in the eyes of one people and few to appear as many in the eyes of another people. If He covers the inner sight baṣīra of a people the sharpness of their physical eyes abṣār will not benefit them. In that there is a lesson and a warning for those of insight to realize that the help of Allah can come to the believers even though they may be few in number; and that defeat can come to those on falsehood even though they may be great in number. (Lo! Herein) in Allah enabling Muhammad to triumph on the Day of Badr (verily is a lesson for those who have eyes) concerning Religion, i.e. the believers; it is also said that this means: it was a lesson for those who saw it with their own eyes.

**A decisive victory in the face of a great difference in resources, and the words a denier took refuge in found to be empty.**

In spite of this, those who denied the truth suffered a crushing defeat and the believers achieved a decisive victory. This is a clear proof that God is always on the side of the believers. In the face of such a great difference in resources, an extraordinary victory cannot be achieved without God’s succour. It is also a clear indication to those who deny the truth of how they are placed in this world. There are obvious signs in the words and deeds of the preacher that the Truth he preaches comes from God. They live by false explanations, until finally they leave for the next world, only to learn that the words in which they had taken refuge were utterly meaningless from the standpoint of reality.

**An example of a prophecy fulfilled, a small group scoring a victory, and a token for the prophethood of Muhammad.**

Now, cited in this verse is an example of how the prophecy has been fulfilled. To sum up, it can be safely said that making a small group of people with very little to fight against a much stronger group and score a victory, as prophesied in Makkah, is an unusual event full of lessons for the observant and the discerning. You had a sign for the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ in the form of two groups-that of Muhammad and that of Abu Sufyan-who met on the Day of Badr. One group (Muhammad ﷺ and his Companions) fought in obedience of Allah, and the other group consisted of unbelievers in Allah and His Messenger (Abu Sufyan and his group).
